blocks.text: Hedging is used to reduce or eliminate the risk of price fluctuation. It involves taking an opposite position in the futures market to what you have in the spot market.

items: Long Hedge (Buy Futures): Used by IMPORTERS. If you have to pay dollars in the future, you fear the dollar price will go up. You buy futures today to lock in the price.
Short Hedge (Sell Futures): Used by EXPORTERS. If you will receive dollars in the future, you fear the dollar price will fall. You sell futures today to lock in the profit.

blocks.text: Speculators take risks to make profits based on their market view. They do not have an underlying exposure like importers/exporters.

items: Bullish View: If you expect the USD/INR rate to rise, you BUY Currency Futures.
Bearish View: If you expect the USD/INR rate to fall, you SELL Currency Futures.

blocks.text: Arbitrage involves making risk-free profit by exploiting price differences between the Spot market and the Futures market.
Cash & Carry Arbitrage: When Futures are 'overpriced', you Buy Spot and Sell Futures simultaneously to lock in the difference.
Spread trading involves buying one contract and selling another contract of a different maturity (e.g., Buy January Future + Sell February Future).
Key Benefit: Spread trades have lower risk compared to naked positions, so exchanges charge lower margins for them.
